6) State Transition Function: The environment evolves according to the transition function
\mathcal { P } ( \mathcal { S } _ { t + 1 } \mid \mathcal { S } _ { t } , \: \mathbf { A } _ { t } ) ,
which jointly captures (i) the clearing results of the P2P market, (ii) the physical power balance and ESS dynamics in (8), and (iii) exogenous uncertainties such as renewable variability and load fluctuations. This transition rules how local actions collectively shape the global system evolution.
7) Discount Factor: The discount factor
\gamma \in ( 0 , 1 )
determines each agent’s preference over future rewards.
C. LSTM-MAPPO with CTDE Training Method
In this work, the LSTM-MAPPO algorithm is presented to address P2P trading problem among N microgrids. The LSTM-MAPPO framework consists of N decentralized policy networks, denoted by
\{ \pi _ { \theta _ { i } } \} _ { i = 1 } ^ { N }
, and critic networks
\{ V _ { \phi _ { i } } \} _ { i = 1 } ^ { N } ,
which are used to approximate the policy and value functions of the microgrids, respectively.
Each agent i selects the action
\mathcal { A } _ { t } ^ { i }
based on local observation
\mathcal { O } _ { t } ^ { i }
and the policy
\pi _ { \theta _ { i } }
to maximize the discounted cumulative reward
J ^ { i } ( \theta _ { i } )
and learn a value function
V _ { \phi _ { i } }
based on the global observation
\mathcal { O } _ { t }
. The policy
\pi _ { \theta _ { i } }
of agent i is updated by minimizing the following loss function:
\begin{aligned} { \mathcal { L } _ { \sf { a c t o r } } ( \theta _ { i } ) = } & { { } - \frac { 1 } { B } \sum _ { l = 1 } ^ { B } \Big [ \operatorname* { m i n } \bigl ( \rho _ { \theta _ { i } , l } A _ { l } ^ { i } , \: \operatorname { c l i p } ( \rho _ { \theta _ { i } , l } , \: 1 - \epsilon , \: 1 + \epsilon ) , } \\ { } & { { } \quad A _ { l } ^ { i } \bigr ) \; - \; c \mathcal { H } \bigl ( \pi _ { \theta _ { i } } ( \cdot \mid \mathcal { O } _ { l } ^ { i } ) \bigr ) \Big ] , \quad \ \ \ \ \ ( \tt { a } ) . } \\ \end{aligned}\tag{17}
where
B
is the batch size, c is the entropy parameter, ϵ is the clipping threshold, and
\mathcal { H } [ \cdot ]
is the entropy of the policy distribution, and
\rho _ { \theta _ { i } , l }
is the importance sampling ratio
\rho _ { \theta _ { i } , l } = \frac { \pi _ { \theta _ { i } } \big ( \mathcal { A } _ { t } ^ { i } | \mathcal { O } _ { t } ^ { i } \big ) } { \pi _ { \theta _ { i } ^ { \mathsf { o l d } } } \big ( \mathcal { A } _ { t } ^ { i } | \mathcal { O } _ { t } ^ { i } \big ) } ,\tag{18}
where
\pi _ { \theta _ { i } ^ { \mathrm { o l d } } }
denotes the old policy of agent i used to generate the samples in the current batch. And the advantage
A _ { l } ^ { i }
is computed by Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE):
\hat { A } _ { l } ^ { i } = \sum _ { t = 0 } ^ { T - 1 } ( \gamma \lambda ) ^ { t } \left( \mathcal { R } _ { l + t } ^ { i } + \gamma V _ { \phi _ { i } } ( s _ { i , l + t + 1 } ) - V _ { \phi _ { i } } ( s _ { i , l + t } ) \right) ,\tag{19}
where λ denotes the GAE parameter. The critic is updated by minimizing the regression error between the predicted value and the GAE–based target. The critic loss for agent i is defined as
\mathcal { L } _ { \sf c r i t i c } ( \phi _ { i } ) = \frac { 1 } { B } \sum _ { l = 1 } ^ { B } \left( V _ { \phi _ { i } } ( \mathcal { O } _ { l } ^ { i } ) \; - \; \hat { V } _ { l } ^ { i } \right) ^ { 2 } ,\tag{20}
where
\hat { V } _ { l } ^ { i } = A _ { l } ^ { i } + V _ { \phi _ { i } } ^ { \mathrm { o l d } } ( \mathcal { O } _ { l } ^ { i } )
is the target constructed from the GAE and the baseline value while
V _ { \phi _ { i } } ^ { \mathrm { o l d } }
denotes the old critic network of agent i when the samples were collected. Given the learning rates α
θ
and
\alpha _ { \phi }
, the parameters of policy and critic networks of agent i are updated based on gradient information:
\begin{aligned} { \theta _ { i } } & { { } \leftarrow \theta _ { i } - \alpha _ { \theta } \operatorname { \nabla } _ { \theta _ { i } } \mathcal { L } _ { \sf { a c t o r } } ( \theta _ { i } ) , } \\ { \phi _ { i } } & { { } \leftarrow \phi _ { i } - \alpha _ { \phi } \operatorname { \nabla } _ { \phi _ { i } } \mathcal { L } _ { \sf { c r i t i c } } ( \phi _ { i } ) . } \\ \end{aligned}\tag{21}
To enhance temporal representation, an LSTM module is incorporated for sequential observation embedding, while a sinusoidal periodic encoder is employed to capture daily cyclical patterns. The overall training process of MMAPPO is summarized in Algorithm 3. For further architectural and implementation details of the policy and critic networks, readers are referred to [12].
